title: Toddler Sleep: Routines and Naps
hook: Toddlers (1–2 years) typically need 11–14 hours of sleep per 24 hours, naps included. A predictable bedtime routine does more for sleep than almost anything else.
key_points: Toddlers 1–2 years generally need about 11–14 hours of total sleep in 24 hours, counting naps.
Naps gradually consolidate and shorten with age, and many toddlers move from two naps to one.
A short, predictable wind-down routine — like brush, book, bed — signals the body it's time to sleep.
Bedtime stalling and resistance are common; consistent times and limits help more than negotiating.
content_html: Sleep needs are big in the toddler years. The American Academy of Sleep Medicine, whose guidelines the AAP endorses, recommends about 11–14 hours of total sleep per 24 hours for children aged 1–2 — and that total includes naps, so daytime sleep counts toward it. As toddlers grow, naps tend to consolidate and shorten, and many make the shift from two naps a day to one.
extra_html: The most reliable lever for good sleep is a predictable routine. A short, calming wind-down — the AAP often describes a simple "brush, book, bed" sequence — cues the body that sleep is coming, and keeping bedtimes and wake times consistent helps a child feel secure. Bedtime stalling, the famous "one more story," and outright resistance are all common at this age; steady routines and gentle, consistent limits tend to work better than nightly negotiations. This is general guidance; if your toddler's sleep is a persistent worry, talk to your pediatrician.

related.title: When Good Sleep Suddenly Gets Worse
related.hook: Sleep that was going well can fall apart around growth spurts, teething, travel, or illness. These rough patches are normal, they pass, and a steady routine helps you ride them out.

related.title: A Safe Sleep Space for Baby
related.hook: Pediatric guidance for safer infant sleep is simple: a firm, flat surface with nothing in it — no pillows, blankets, bumpers, or soft toys.

flashcards.prompt: Roughly how much total sleep do toddlers (1–2 years) typically need per 24 hours?
flashcards.explanation_html: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine, endorsed by the AAP, recommends roughly 11–14 hours per 24 hours for 1–2 year-olds, counting daytime naps.

flashcards.prompt: What's one of the most effective tools for smoother toddler bedtimes?
flashcards.back_html: A short, predictable wind-down routine (such as brush, book, bed) plus consistent bedtimes. Routine and consistency help more than nightly negotiation.
